title: न्यायदर्शनदिशा ईश्वरस्वरूपविमर्शः Nyadarshandisha Ishwarswarupbimarsha
nepali: दर्शनक्षेत्रे नैकमतमीश्वरविषये । भूतवादिनश्चार्वाकाः बौद्धाश्च दर्शनेतरैः स्वीकृतमीश्वरं नाङ्गीकुर्वन्ति । जैनाश्च प्रमाणत्वेनेश्वरमस्वीकुर्वन्ति । अन्यानि चास्तिकानि दर्शनान्यपि ईश्वरस्वरूपादिविषयं स्वानुकूलतया प्रतिपादयन्ति । परन्तु न्यायदर्शनेन जगद्रूप–महत्कार्यस्य कारणरूपेण स्वीकृतो वर्तत ईश्वरः । ‘तेन विना तृणाग्रमपि न चलति’ इत्यनुसारेण जगत्सृष्ट्यादिकार्यं सर्वमपि ईश्वरः सम्पादयतीति शास्त्राणि उद्घोषयन्ति, न्यायदर्शनं च । न्यायदर्शनेन महता प्रयत्नेन विप्रतिपत्तयो निरस्य ईश्वरस्यास्तित्वं दृढीकृतम् । सोऽयमीश्वरः निमित्तकारणमेवेति वदन्ति नैयायिकाः । तत्र निमित्तकारणत्वमङ्गीकृतस्य तस्य स्वरूप–सामथ्र्य–ज्ञानादिविषयाः ज्ञातव्या भवन्ति । ईश्वरसम्बद्धविषयस्य गाम्भीर्यं विशदव्याख्यामपेक्षते, तथाऽपि प्रस्तुतनिबन्धे विषयेऽस्मिन् संक्षिप्ततया अध्ययनं विधीयते ।)
american_english: In philosophy, there is no unanimity regarding God. The materialists (Charvakas) and Buddhists — systems outside the fold — do not accept God as accepted by others. The Jains too do not accept God as authoritative. Other theistic systems also expound on the nature of God and related matters according to their own views. But in Nyaya philosophy, God is accepted as the cause of the world-form, the great effect. As the saying goes, "without Him not even a blade of grass moves"; the scriptures proclaim that all actions from the creation of the world onward are accomplished by God, and so does Nyaya philosophy. Nyaya philosophy, with great effort, having removed objections, has established the existence of God. The Naiyayikas say that this God is only the efficient cause. Of that God whose efficient causality is accepted, matters such as His nature, capability and knowledge must be known. The gravity of the subject related to God calls for detailed explanation, but in the present paper a brief study of this subject is conducted.
british_english: In philosophy, views on God are not unanimous. The materialists (Charvakas) and Buddhists, systems outside the orthodox fold, do not accept God as accepted elsewhere. The Jains too do not accept God as authoritative. Other theistic systems likewise propound their views on the nature of God and so on, according to their own persuasion. But in Nyaya philosophy, God is accepted as the cause of the world-form—the great effect. As it is said, "without Him not even a blade of grass moves": the scriptures proclaim that all works, from world-creation onward, are accomplished by God, and so does Nyaya philosophy. Nyaya philosophy, with great effort and having set aside objections, has established the existence of God. The Naiyayikas say that this God is only the efficient cause. Of that God whose efficient causality is accepted, questions such as His nature, capability and knowledge must be known. The seriousness of the subject relating to God calls for detailed explanation, but the present paper undertakes a brief study of this subject.
australian_english: In philosophy, there's no agreement on God. The materialists (Charvakas) and Buddhists — outside systems — don't accept God as others do. The Jains don't accept God as authoritative either. Other theistic systems also have their say about the nature of God and such, each to its own view. But in Nyaya philosophy, God is accepted as the cause of the world-form, the great effect. As the saying goes, "without Him not even a blade of grass moves"; the scriptures reckon everything from the creation of the world onwards is done by God, and so does Nyaya philosophy. Nyaya philosophy has, with great effort, removed objections and established that God exists. The Naiyayikas say this God is only the efficient cause. Of that God whose efficient causality is accepted, things like His nature, capability and knowledge need to be known. The subject of God is weighty and calls for detailed explanation, but this paper gives it a brief study.
informal_english: In philosophy, there's no one view on God. The materialists (Charvakas) and Buddhists — they don't accept God like others do. The Jains too don't accept God as valid. Other theistic schools also explain God's nature in their own way. But Nyaya philosophy accepts God as the cause of the world, the great effect. As the saying goes, "without Him not even a blade of grass moves"; the shastras proclaim that everything from the creation of the world is done by God, and Nyaya says the same. Nyaya philosophy, after great effort and removing objections, has established God's existence. The Naiyayikas say this God is only the efficient cause. Of that God whose efficient causality is accepted, His nature, capability, knowledge etc. must be known. The subject concerning God is serious and needs detailed explanation, but the present paper does a brief study of it.
